
=================================================================
#13 Pumsuk  (641)
Arc: The Five Principles · place: surabol · tone: K-drama romance
Logline: Pumsuk asks for the girl. Chunchu asks for something else.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Pumsuk asks for the girl. Chunchu asks for something else.
[1] ── SCENE: The Study ──
[2] ¶ Chunchu receives him in the study, not the hall. A go game sits half-played between them. Chunchu is wiping his hands on a cloth, slowly, both sides. He has not been doing anything to dirty them.
[3] Kim Pumsuk: Sir. I— I have come about Lady Gotaso. / With your permission, I would like— that is, I would ask—
[4] King Muyeol: Sit. You’re making the stones nervous. / She told me at breakfast. Four children, all named. She is very thorough. She gets that from me.
[5] Kim Pumsuk: …Then you consent, sir?
[6] King Muyeol: I consent to the girl. She was never mine to keep. / Do you know what the yard teaches, Hwarang? Five rules. / Here is a sixth.
[7] ¶ Munhee is in the doorway. She has been there the whole time. Pumsuk only notices now, which tells you something about Pumsuk.
[8] Munhee: Don’t make him swear.
[9] King Muyeol: …Why not.
[10] Munhee: If he keeps it, it was owed anyway. If he cannot, it kills him.
[11] ¶ He makes him swear. It is the only time in this record that Chunchu misreads a room, and it is the room with his daughter in it.
[12] King Muyeol: If anything happens to her, you know I’m going to kill you, right? Haha...
[13] ¶ He laughs. He puts the cloth down. Pumsuk has heard, the way all of Surabol has heard, about a certain ford. Nobody else in the room is laughing.
[14] Kim Pumsuk: On my life, I will protect Lady Gotaso!
[15] ── SCENE: The Wedding ──
[16] ¶ At the back of the hall, the Queen watches her great-niece marry for love.
[17] [WEDDING Gotaso + Kim Pumsuk]
[18] ▼ FLASHBACK 625 the girl-child
    [18.0] ¶ **Munhee** does not watch the vows. She watches the doorway and remembers a different night in the same house: the girl-child arriving, pink silk already too sure of itself, Chunchu’s hand huge around a wrist that would never learn to be still. They named her **Gotaso** when the lantern-band was the same shape it is tonight.
[18] ▲ end flashback
[19] Queen Sunduk: …Your son’s girl. / That doorway has taken three of this house now.
[20] [CARD Princess Chunmyung: The Queen’s elder sister, and Chunchu’s mother. She gave up a throne to marry for love.]
[21] Princess Chunmyung: Four. If Your Majesty counts honestly.
[22] Queen Sunduk: …I count honestly.
[23] Gotaso: We will be happy forever!
[24] ── SCENE: The Wedding Night ──
[25] Kim Pumsuk: …My lady. Your hands are cold. / But the back of your neck… is hot.
[26] Gotaso: Because I am shaking. / And… because yours are too warm. / The hand at my waist. / Don’t take it away.
[27] Kim Pumsuk: Are you frightened? / If I… come closer.
[28] Gotaso: No. / Because I want to be somewhere with nobody in it. / Look at me once more.
[29] ¶ Behind the doors the feast falls away.
[30] ── SCENE: The Empty Hall ──
[31] ¶ The hall empties. The Queen does not leave, and neither does the Marshal. Neither of them has ever been the first to leave a room.
[32] ¶ She has had twenty years to learn the back of his neck: the place the armour strap has worn shiny, the two grey hairs at his temple that were not there before the last campaign. Tonight the hall is empty and nobody is writing anything down, so she looks at all of it.
[33] ¶ Color rises along her throat. She keeps her mouth closed so the breath will not give her away. He does not turn. That is the only mercy left in the room.
[34] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty.
[35] Queen Sunduk: …Not that word. Not tonight.
[36] Kim Yushin: Then what am I to call you.
[37] Queen Sunduk: Don’t call me anything.
[38] ¶ He takes one step. It is the smallest thing he does in this entire record and it costs him longer than any battle in it.
[39] Kim Yushin: Today you watched your niece marry the man she loves. / I watched your face the entire time. / Your Majesty—
[40] Queen Sunduk: Yushin.
[41] Kim Yushin: …You said my name.
[42] Queen Sunduk: So stop.
[43] Kim Yushin: One sentence. Let me have one. / Two horses. Tonight would be enough. / Three days to the border. After three days we are nobody at all.
[44] ¶ She reaches up. He is very still, the way a man is still when he has already decided not to be the one who moves. Her fingers find his mouth before the rest of the sentence can.
[45] Queen Sunduk: Don’t say it. / If you say it, I have to hear it for the rest of my life.
[46] Kim Yushin: Then hear it for the rest of your life.
[47] ¶ For a moment she does not answer, and the moment is long enough that both of them will spend years deciding what it meant.
[48] ¶ Her fingers are still on his mouth. He does not take the next step. The lamp between them does the looking. When she speaks again she is already Queen.
[49] Queen Sunduk: …Without you this country does not last half a year.
[50] Kim Yushin: You are talking about the country.
[51] Queen Sunduk: Because the country is the only thing I am permitted to talk about.
[52] ¶ She is close enough now to count what it is costing him. She counts it. Then she takes her hand back and puts it where a queen’s hand goes.
[53] Queen Sunduk: One more step and I do not stop.
[54] Kim Yushin: …Then I will not take it.
[55] Queen Sunduk: Thank you.
[56] Kim Yushin: Don’t thank me. / That is the sound you make when you have won.
[57] Queen Sunduk: …Then neither of us has.
[58] ¶ He steps back into the shape of a subject. It fits, because he has worn it twenty years. It has never once fit.
[59] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty.
[60] Queen Sunduk: …Yes. That will do.
[61] ¶ Neither of them mentions that night again. Thirty-two years later, on the last day of his life, he is asked whether he ever wanted anything for himself, and the record notes only that he took some time to answer.
[62] ── SCENE: The Road to Daeya ──
[63] ¶ Three days later the couple leave for **Daeya Fortress**, where Pumsuk has just been named Guardian. She waves from the cart until the capital is out of sight; he rides beside the wheel the whole way. Daeya is a border post. Nobody at the wedding said the word _border_ out loud.
[64] [PLACE daeya: A border post with a fine view of Baekje. The view works both ways.]
[65] ¶ Her parents stand at the gate until the dust settles. Then a little longer.
[66] King Muyeol: She waved the whole way. Like someone I know.
[67] Munhee: I never waved at you. I was busy sewing.
[68] King Muyeol: …So you do remember.
[69] Munhee: Don’t you start. Not at the gate.
[70] ¶ **“Dear… have you already forgotten how we met?” Munhee hasn’t. It involves a dream, a skirt, and a coat torn on purpose…!**
